blindSummary:
An associated self-governing territory of a distant metropolitan state: the metropolitan state's federal protections apply; small tourism economy; thin data.

Underlying evidence base is that of the metropolitan state, adapted for local conditions.
blindOutOfScope: Dependent territory of a distant metropolitan state; local deviations noted in the summary.
blindSourceSummaries: A trans-equality advocacy group's know-your-rights guide to airport security - body-scanner flags, pat-downs, documentation mismatches, and how to request alternative screening - relevant to this territory because the metropolitan state's airport-security authority operates here.

An international rights group (Mar 2026): one of the metropolitan state's constituent states is revoking gender-affirming identification — metropolitan document-policy context relevant to the territory.

Foreign public broadcaster (Feb 2014): methodology piece behind an interactive LGBT legal-status map and timeline produced with a UN human-rights office and an international LGBTI federation, categorising states by legal status (context for the territory, whose legal status derives from the metropolitan state).

Territory public law signed January 2023: amends the territory's code of laws to provide criteria for enhanced sentencing of defendants for hate-motivated crimes - the hate-crimes statute covering sexual orientation and gender identity.

Equality-monitoring project's policy profile for this territory: LGBTQ policy scores - sexual orientation 4/23 (Low), gender identity -2/26 (Negative), overall 2/49; marriage recognition exists but no second-parent adoption, no family-services nondiscrimination, no assisted-reproduction recognition.

Encyclopedia-mirror overview of LGBT rights in this territory: same-sex marriage legal since 2015 (a metropolitan supreme-court ruling extending marriage equality applies to the territory), no criminalisation, limited territorial-level protections.
